---
title: "Bet selection: three families of rule, and where the edge is not"
subtitle: "Paper 6 in a series on UK All-Weather racing outcomes"
author: "Patrick Gillen"
date: "2026-09-10"
abstract: |
  A betting rule has three parts: which horse to back, which races to bet on
  the strength of the model's output, and which races to bet on the strength
  of the race itself. Two earlier rounds searched the first two and found
  nothing that beat the rule paper 1 took from Owen. This paper adds the
  third: filters on field size, class, course, distance and going, all known
  the night before the race. Every candidate in all three families then had
  to rank in the top decile of its family on both halves of the search window
  before it could reach the test split. That guard struck Owen's rule on
  three of the four markets. It did not save the search. One rule topped every
  search-set table, backing the horse whose model probability most exceeds its
  market probability in fields of eleven to twelve runners, at
  `r local({ S <- file.path(rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj")), "_targets_p6"); d <- targets::tar_read(p6_round3_ranks, store = S)$table; r <- d[d$bet == "win" & d$rule == "P4 / field size 11-12", ]; sprintf("%+.1f%%", 100 * r$val_roi) })`
  on the win market with the two halves of the window two points apart. On the
  test split it returned
  `r local({ S <- file.path(rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj")), "_targets_p6"); d <- targets::tar_read(p6_round3_ranks, store = S)$table; r <- d[d$bet == "win" & d$rule == "P4 / field size 11-12", ]; sprintf("%+.1f%%", 100 * r$test_roi) })`.
  Search-set rank predicts test rank negatively on all four markets. Two
  thirds to four fifths of the variation in return between rules is explained
  by the mean price the rule backs, so a leaderboard mostly ranks price bands,
  and the residual does not hold across halves of one window. The two best
  rules on test were the two carried forward without being selected: the
  market favourite in every race, with no model in it, and Owen's rule. Three
  rules in the shortlist are profitable once the bookmaker's margin is
  removed; none is profitable with it in place. Paper 4 showed the model ties
  the settled starting price and beats the overnight forecast price, so its
  value sits between them, and every backtest in this series settles at the
  closing end of that interval. The final section sets out what that implies
  for live use.
format:
  html: default
  pdf:
    toc: true
    number-sections: true
bibliography: references.bib
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(targets)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(glue)

# Paper 6 reads the paper-6 store. Like papers 4 and 5 and unlike papers 1-3
# this does NOT call tar_config_set(): that writes the project-root
# `_targets.yaml`, which papers 1-3's own setup chunks also write, and
# pointing it at `_targets_p6` would send their next render at the wrong
# store. Passing `store =` per call leaves `_targets.yaml` untouched.
P6_ROOT <- rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj"))
P6_STORE <- file.path(P6_ROOT, "_targets_p6")

source(file.path(P6_ROOT, "papers", "06_betting_strategy", "_helpers.R"))

# tar_load() centrally so tarchetypes::tar_quarto() picks these up as render
# dependencies — files pulled in via {{< include >}} are not auto-scanned.
tar_load(c(
  # universe, gates, provenance
  p6_universe, p6_search_set_check, p6_fit_provenance_tbl, p6_ledger_gate,
  p6_sweep_gate, p6_round3_gate,
  # what was searched (_01)
  p6_explore_bets, p6_explore_grid, p6_rc_all_specs, p6_rc_pruned,
  p6_rc_kept, p6_rc_terciles, p6_agree_max, p6_agree_owen,
  # what was found (_02)
  p6_val_sweep, p6_rc_sweep_full, p6_comb_sweep_full, p6_rc_best_pairs,
  p6_rc_guard, p6_thr_guard, p6_comb_guard, p6_guard_summary,
  p6_guard_summary_sub, p6_owen_guard, p6_round3_shortlists,
  p6_round3_val, p6_round3_test, p6_round3_ranks, p6_explore_ranks,
  # price band (_03)
  p6_price_band_fit, p6_price_context,
  # staking (_04)
  p6_staking_test, p6_staking_val, p6_stage3_rules,
  # descriptive
  p6_field_sizes_val, p6_field_sizes_test, p6_overround_val,
  p6_eachway_terms_decision
), store = P6_STORE)

BET_LAB <- p6_bet_labels()
```
